Let the four two-digit numbers be

\[
10a_1+b_1,\quad 10a_2+b_2,\quad 10a_3+b_3,\quad 10a_4+b_4
\]

where all eight digits \(a_i,b_i\) are distinct nonzero digits. Since there are 9 possible nonzero digits \(1,\dots,9\), exactly one digit is missing.

Let the missing digit be \(m\).

The sum of all digits \(1+2+\cdots+9=45\), so the sum of the eight used digits is

\[
45-m.
\]

Let

\[
A=a_1+a_2+a_3+a_4
\]

be the sum of the tens digits, and

\[
B=b_1+b_2+b_3+b_4
\]

be the sum of the units digits. Then

\[
A+B=45-m.
\]

The sum of the four two-digit numbers is

\[
10A+B=221.
\]

Substitute \(B=45-m-A\):

\[
10A+45-m-A=221
\]

\[
9A+45-m=221
\]

\[
9A=176+m.
\]

Thus \(176+m\) must be divisible by \(9\). Since \(176\equiv 5\pmod 9\), we need

\[
5+m\equiv 0\pmod 9,
\]

so

\[
m\equiv 4\pmod 9.
\]

The only digit from \(1\) to \(9\) satisfying this is

\[
m=4.
\]

Indeed, one possible set is \(13,25,86,97\), whose sum is \(221\) and whose digits use every digit except \(4\).

The answer is 4.
